_meta.indication: Treatment of symptomatic or progressive medullary thyroid cancer in patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic disease

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, international, randomized (2:1), double-blind, placebo-controlled study
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with unresectable locally advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC)
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Progression-free survival (PFS) as determined by central (independent) review
pivotal_trials.result: Statistically significant PFS improvement; HR 0.35 (95% CI 0.24, 0.53); p<0.0001; median PFS 16.4 months (placebo) vs not reached (22.6 months, NE) for vandetanib

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions (>20%): diarrhea, rash, acne, nausea, hypertension, headache, fatigue, decreased appetite, abdominal pain. Serious: QT prolongation, Torsades de pointes, sudden death. Diarrhea/colitis 57% and hypertension 33% on vandetanib.
target_moa: Kinase inhibitor that inhibits tyrosine kinases including EGFR family, VEGF receptors, and RET

boxed_warning.content: QT prolongation, Torsades de pointes, and sudden death; vandetanib should not be used in patients with hypocalcemia, hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia, or long QT syndrome

rems.type: Vandetanib REMS Program: restricted distribution; only prescribers and pharmacies certified with the program can prescribe/dispense, due to risk of QT prolongation, Torsades de pointes, and sudden death

advisory_committee.vote: Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee met December 2, 2010; voted 10 to 0 (Yes=10, No=0, Abstain=0) that if there is a population in which the risk-benefit profile is acceptable, additional doses of vandetanib should be evaluated as a post-marketing requirement to determine the optimal dose

description.text: Labeling update to include updated overall survival data from Study D4200C00058, carcinogenicity data, and PLLR-format pregnancy/lactation changes (no new indication)

citations.quote: - To the CLINICAL STUDIES section (14) to include updated overall survival (OS) data from Study D4200C00058 that was used to satisfy and fulfill the requirements for Postmarketing Requirement (PMR) 1719-4 (Fulfilled April 27, 2017).

orphan_indication.text: Vandetanib has orphan drug exclusivity for the medullary thyroid cancer indication; a pediatric waiver was granted based on vandetanib's orphan drug status

citations.quote: Not applicable. Vandetanib has orphan drug exclusivity for this indication.
Vandetanib has not been studied in a pediatric population. A pediatric waiver was granted by the Pediatric Review Committee based on vandetanib's orphan drug status.

summary.text: Vandetanib was approved for medullary thyroid cancer based on a single randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase III trial (Study 58) showing significant PFS improvement; the application was discussed at the December 2, 2010 ODAC; a REMS with elements to assure safe use was required for QT risk; and the drug has orphan drug exclusivity for this indication.

citations.quote: The recommendation for approval is based on the single, randomized clinical trial in which vandetanib showed a statistically significant progression free survival advantage compared to placebo in patients with locally advanced or metastatic medullary thyroid cancer (MTC).
This application is based on one Phase III trial (Study D4200C00058 or Study 58) and two uncontrolled single-arm Phase II studies (D4200C00008 and D4200C00068).
the application was presented at the December 2, 2010 Oncologic Drugs Advisory Committee.

Pursuant to 505-1(f)(1), we have determined that vandetanib can be approved only if elements necessary to assure safe use are required as part of a REMS to mitigate the risks of QT prolongation, Torsades de pointes, and sudden death that are listed in the labeling.
Not applicable. Vandetanib has orphan drug exclusivity for this indication.

requirement.text: 1719-1: Conduct a long-term (2 year) rodent carcinogenicity study in the rat (with SPA of protocol prior to initiation)

citations.quote: 1719-1 To evaluate the potential for a serious risk of carcinogenicity, conduct a long-term (2 year) rodent carcinogenicity study in the rat. Submit the carcinogenicity protocol for a Special Protocol Assessment prior to initiating the study.

requirement.text: 1719-2: Conduct a rodent carcinogenicity study in the mouse (with SPA of protocol prior to initiation)

citations.quote: 1719-2 To evaluate the potential for a serious risk of carcinogenicity, conduct a rodent carcinogenicity study in the mouse. Submit the carcinogenicity protocol for a Special Protocol Assessment prior to initiating the study.

requirement.text: 1719-3: Conduct a randomized dose-finding trial in progressive or symptomatic MTC patients randomized to vandetanib 300 mg or 150 mg daily, with safety assessments including vortex keratopathy, corneal stromal changes, and heart failure; primary endpoint overall response rate

citations.quote: 1719-3 Conduct a randomized dose-finding trial in which patients with progressive or symptomatic medullary thyroid cancer will be randomized to vandetanib 300 mg or 150 mg daily. The trial will include analyses of the safety and activity of the 150 mg dose of vandetanib. Safety assessments will include evaluations of vortex keratopathy and corneal stromal changes, with ophthalmology examination every 6 months with corneal photographs of abnormalities. Safety assessments will also include evaluation of heart failure using serial echocardiograms in all patients. A primary endpoint will include overall response rate.

requirement.text: 1719-4: Submit the results of the final analysis of overall survival data from the randomized trial of vandetanib 300 mg vs. placebo (Study 58)

citations.quote: 1719-4 Submit the results of the final analysis of overall survival data from the randomized clinical trial of vandetanib 300 mg vs. placebo in medullary thyroid cancer (Study 58).
